newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's GrandAir sees 96 sales over 1.0 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Manila's GrandAir sees 96 sales over 1.0 bln pesos.

text.p: Philippines' Grand International Airways (GrandAir) said on Monday it is expecting sales to reach more than one billion pesos this year.
The country's second air carrier posted 380 million peso in sales at the end of last year, six months after it begun operation.

"GrandAir expects sales to grow at a yearly 30 percent rate. Thus, requiring shareholders to inject 300 million to 500 million pesos within the next two years to sustain hefty growth of capital values," the company said in a statement.
Major stockholders are members of the Panlilio family who are involved in hotel and real estate ventures in the Philippines.

GrandAir is one of several new airlines that have opened in the Philippines after it recently liberalised the aviation sector. The unlisted GrandAir offers cheaper plane fares than Philippine Airlines, the country's main airline.
At present, GrandAir has four Airbus A300s and one Boeing 737. Four additional Boeing 737s are expected to be delivered by mid-November.
